regions.Ann Arbor, Lansing and Flint: Pair with Detroit or do it on the way: the university museums of Ann Arbor, Zaha Hadid's Broad Art Museum and the restored capitol in Lansing, Flint's art museum and Bavarian Frankenmuth.
regions.Detroit and Southeast Michigan: Give Detroit two or three days. Rivera's murals at the DIA, the Art Deco Guardian and Fisher buildings, Motown's Studio A and Eastern Market on a Saturday, then a full day at The Henry Ford and Greenfield Village in Dearborn and an afternoon at Saarinen's Cranbrook.
regions.Grand Rapids and the Lake Michigan shore: Meijer Gardens and Wright's Meyer May House in Grand Rapids, the Ford Museum, then the lakeshore towns of Holland and Saugatuck and the dunes and lighthouse at Ludington.
regions.Mackinac and the Upper Peninsula: A long trip north. Cross the Mackinac Bridge, take the ferry to car-free Mackinac Island, watch freighters at the Soo Locks, then Tahquamenon Falls, Pictured Rocks by boat and the copper country of the Keweenaw.
regions.Sleeping Bear and Traverse Bay: Michigan's finest landscape: the Dune Climb and the Pierce Stocking drive at Sleeping Bear, Glen Haven and Leland's Fishtown, Point Betsie, and in October the Tunnel of Trees north of Harbor Springs.
regions.Southwest Michigan: The closest corner of Michigan: climb Warren Dunes, then the car and aviation collections and the art museum around Kalamazoo. An easy two-day loop.

sites.name: Detroit Institute of Arts
sites.desc: One of the great American art museums, with Diego Rivera's Detroit Industry murals (1932 to 1933) filling its central court.

sites.name: Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History
sites.desc: One of the largest museums of African American history, in Midtown next to the DIA.
sites.wiki: Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History

sites.name: Detroit Historical Museum
sites.desc: City history from fur trade to auto industry, with a reconstructed Streets of Old Detroit and an assembly line.

sites.name: Museum of Contemporary Art Detroit
sites.desc: A non-collecting contemporary art space in a former car dealership on Woodward Avenue.

sites.name: Motown Museum (Hitsville U.S.A.)
sites.desc: The house where Berry Gordy founded Motown in 1959, with Studio A where the Supremes and Marvin Gaye recorded.

sites.name: Guardian Building
sites.desc: Wirt Rowland's 1929 Art Deco skyscraper with a banking hall of Pewabic and Rookwood tile, open to visitors.

sites.name: Fisher Building
sites.desc: Albert Kahn's 1928 tower in New Center, with a painted barrel-vaulted arcade that Detroiters call the city's largest art object.

sites.name: Michigan Central Station
sites.desc: The 1913 Beaux-Arts station, long a symbol of Detroit's decline, restored by Ford and reopened in 2024.

sites.name: Lafayette Park
sites.desc: Mies van der Rohe's residential towers and townhouses (1958 to 1965) in a park by Ludwig Hilberseimer and Alfred Caldwell, the largest collection of Mies buildings anywhere.

sites.name: Fox Theatre
sites.desc: C. Howard Crane's 1928 movie palace, an opulent fantasy of Asian and Egyptian motifs, still a working theater.

sites.name: Heidelberg Project
sites.desc: Tyree Guyton's outdoor art environment of painted houses and found objects on the East Side.

sites.name: Eastern Market
sites.desc: One of the largest historic public markets in the country, busiest on Saturday mornings, with murals all around.

sites.name: Pewabic Pottery
sites.desc: The Arts and Crafts pottery founded in 1903 by Mary Chase Perry Stratton, still making its iridescent tile.

sites.name: Belle Isle Park
sites.desc: An island park in the Detroit River planned by Olmsted, with the Anna Scripps Whitcomb Conservatory and the Dossin Great Lakes Museum.

sites.name: Ford Piquette Avenue Plant
sites.desc: The 1904 factory where the Model T was designed and first built, now a museum.

sites.name: Cranbrook
sites.desc: Eliel Saarinen's campus in Bloomfield Hills, with the Cranbrook Art Museum, Saarinen House and Carl Milles sculpture in the gardens.

sites.name: Edsel and Eleanor Ford House
sites.desc: A Cotswold-style estate on Lake St. Clair by Albert Kahn, with grounds by Jens Jensen.

sites.name: Henry Ford Museum of American Innovation
sites.desc: In Dearborn, with the Rosa Parks bus, the Kennedy limousine and a huge collection of American machines and design.

sites.name: Greenfield Village
sites.desc: Henry Ford's open-air museum of relocated American buildings, from Edison's Menlo Park lab to the Wright brothers' cycle shop.

sites.name: Ford Rouge Factory Tour
sites.desc: Albert Kahn's vast River Rouge complex, where you can watch F-150 trucks being assembled.

sites.name: Fair Lane
sites.desc: Henry and Clara Ford's 1915 estate on the Rouge River, with landscape by Jens Jensen.

sites.name: Arab American National Museum
sites.desc: The first museum devoted to Arab American history and culture, in Dearborn.

sites.name: River Raisin National Battlefield Park
sites.desc: Site of the January 1813 battle of the War of 1812 at Monroe.

sites.name: University of Michigan Museum of Art
sites.desc: A large free university art museum in Ann Arbor, with a strong Asian collection.
sites.wiki: University of Michigan Museum of Art

sites.name: Kelsey Museum of Archaeology
sites.desc: The University of Michigan's free museum of Egyptian, Greek, Roman and Near Eastern antiquities.

sites.name: Matthaei Botanical Gardens and Nichols Arboretum
sites.desc: The university's conservatory and gardens, and the Huron River valley arboretum with a famous peony garden.

sites.name: Michigan State Capitol
sites.desc: Elijah Myers's 1879 capitol in Lansing, restored with its painted Victorian interiors and glass floor in the rotunda.

sites.name: Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum
sites.desc: Zaha Hadid's angular steel and glass museum (2012) at Michigan State University, free.
sites.wiki: Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum

sites.name: R.E. Olds Transportation Museum
sites.desc: Oldsmobiles and other Lansing-built vehicles, from the city where Ransom Olds started mass production.

sites.name: Flint Institute of Arts
sites.desc: One of the largest art museums in Michigan, with a notable glass collection.

sites.name: Frankenmuth
sites.desc: A Bavarian-style town famous for chicken dinners and Bronner's enormous Christmas store.

sites.name: Warren Dunes State Park
sites.desc: Dunes rising some 260 feet above Lake Michigan, the closest big Michigan dunes to Champaign.

sites.name: Kalamazoo Institute of Arts
sites.desc: A regional art museum with American art and a strong collection of works on paper.

sites.name: Air Zoo
sites.desc: Aviation and space museum near Kalamazoo, with an SR-71 Blackbird.

sites.name: Gilmore Car Museum
sites.desc: Hundreds of cars displayed in historic barns and a recreated 1930s gas station at Hickory Corners.

sites.name: Kellogg Biological Station Bird Sanctuary
sites.desc: Michigan State University's wetland bird sanctuary on Wintergreen Lake, founded by W. K. Kellogg in 1927.

sites.name: Gerald R. Ford Presidential Museum
sites.region: Grand Rapids and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: The museum of the 38th president on the Grand River, where he and Betty Ford are buried.

sites.name: Frederik Meijer Gardens and Sculpture Park
sites.region: Grand Rapids and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: Gardens and a major sculpture park, with works by Rodin, Moore, Calder and Kusama, and a large Japanese garden.

sites.name: Grand Rapids Art Museum
sites.region: Grand Rapids and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: An art museum in a LEED Gold building by wHY Architecture, host of the ArtPrize festival.

sites.name: Meyer May House
sites.region: Grand Rapids and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1909 Prairie house, restored by Steelcase with its original furniture and art glass. Free tours.

sites.name: Windmill Island and De Zwaan
sites.region: Grand Rapids and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: An 18th-century Dutch windmill shipped from the Netherlands to Holland, Michigan, still grinding flour. Tulip Time is in May.

sites.name: Saugatuck Dunes State Park
sites.region: Grand Rapids and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: Wooded dunes and a quiet beach near the art colony town of Saugatuck.

sites.name: Ludington State Park and Big Sable Point Lighthouse
sites.region: Grand Rapids and the Lake Michigan shore
sites.desc: Dunes, a river and a walk to the black and white Big Sable Point Lighthouse.

sites.name: Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore
sites.desc: Bluffs 450 feet above Lake Michigan, the Dune Climb, the Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive and the Manitou Islands.

sites.name: Glen Haven
sites.desc: A restored lumber-era village with a maritime museum in an old Coast Guard station, inside Sleeping Bear.

sites.name: Fishtown, Leland
sites.desc: Weathered fishing shanties on the Leland River, still a working commercial fishing village.

sites.name: Point Betsie Lighthouse
sites.desc: An 1858 lighthouse on the Lake Michigan shore, among the most photographed in the state.

sites.name: Interlochen Center for the Arts
sites.desc: The arts school and summer camp between two lakes, with summer concerts in its outdoor bowl.

sites.name: Tunnel of Trees
sites.desc: A narrow shoreline road from Harbor Springs to Cross Village under a canopy of trees, glorious in October.

sites.name: Hartwick Pines State Park
sites.desc: One of the last stands of old-growth white pine in the Lower Peninsula, with a logging museum.

sites.name: Mackinac Bridge
sites.desc: David Steinman's five-mile suspension bridge (1957) linking Michigan's two peninsulas.

sites.name: Colonial Michilimackinac
sites.desc: A reconstructed 18th-century French and British fur trading fort at Mackinaw City.

sites.name: Mackinac Island and Fort Mackinac
sites.desc: A car-free island reached by ferry, with horse carriages, Victorian cottages, the Grand Hotel and an 18th-century fort. Driving time is to the ferry at Mackinaw City.

sites.name: Grand Hotel
sites.desc: The 1887 resort hotel with what is billed as the world's longest porch. Driving time is to the ferry at Mackinaw City.

sites.name: Soo Locks
sites.desc: Watch thousand-foot lake freighters rise and fall between Lake Superior and Lake Huron at Sault Ste. Marie.

sites.name: Tahquamenon Falls State Park
sites.desc: Wide amber falls tinted by the tannins of cedar swamps, the Upper Falls among the largest east of the Mississippi.

sites.name: Great Lakes Shipwreck Museum
sites.desc: At Whitefish Point, displaying the bell of the Edmund Fitzgerald, lost nearby in 1975.

sites.name: Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore
sites.desc: Mineral-streaked sandstone cliffs, arches and waterfalls on Lake Superior, best seen by boat or kayak from Munising.

sites.name: Kitch-iti-kipi
sites.desc: Michigan's largest freshwater spring, a clear green pool crossed on a hand-pulled raft.

sites.name: Fayette Historic State Park
sites.desc: A 19th-century iron-smelting ghost town on a limestone harbor of the Garden Peninsula.

sites.name: Keweenaw National Historical Park
sites.desc: The copper country of the Keweenaw Peninsula, with the Quincy Mine hoist and tours underground.

sites.name: Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
sites.desc: Old-growth forest, waterfalls and the Lake of the Clouds overlook on Lake Superior.

sites.name: Isle Royale National Park
sites.desc: A roadless wilderness island in Lake Superior known for its wolves and moose, reached by ferry or seaplane. Driving time is to the ferry at Houghton.
